text:
Josh Doan was one of the reasons to believe in Buffalo this season. Last year, his first with the Sabres after the trade from Utah, Evolving-Hockey had him worth 2.2 wins, 42nd among all forwards, with a play-driving impact in the 97th percentile. This fall he has six points in 21 games, and as the Sabres slide down the power rankings, Sabre Noise put him in the spotlight.

The numbers point two ways. His shooting is fine (four goals on 4.8 expected goals), and the shots are coming from good places. But his five-on-five impact has gone missing: Buffalo takes 47% of the expected goals with him on the ice, more than four points worse than without him, the opposite of last year's story. His scoring rate of 1.13 points per 60 sits well below the 2.08 our talent range expects.

He's 24, the son of Coyotes great Shane Doan, and still drawing more penalties than he takes. A tip-in on the power play against Tampa was a reminder of where he does his damage. The five-on-five share is the number to watch; when it returns, the points usually come with it.
headline: Doan's slow start in a sliding Buffalo
